title: Per-slice changelog entries in landed-changed/, assembled into CHANGELOG.md
lead: A slice no longer edits the changelog. It writes its entry with `slicer changelog add` to its own file under `landed-changed/` (one file per item, named by its ID). At release, `slicer changelog assemble` writes every entry into the Unreleased section in one layout and deletes the files, so parallel landings never touch a shared file. `slicer changelog import` converts an existing Unreleased body into entry files once. Filed 2026-11-11 from the ork relay session; the owner answered Q1 to Q5 on 2026-11-11 (all the recommended options).
findings_note: ork owner 2026-11-11: parallel slice branches that each add a line under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md conflict at nearly every landing (ork runs S132, S173, S204, S226, S244, S255, S257, S263, S267, S223 on 2026-11-08 to 11-11). The owner asked that slicer own a per-slice entry folder named landed-changed and the step that assembles it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Evidence from ork, 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-11:

- Each slice adds a bullet near the top of `## Unreleased` in ork's changelog. Two branches that both add one there change the same lines, so git conflicts and the landing pauses for a hand merge. ork's resolver for this (ork S180, being fixed in ork S327) only patches over it.
- ork's Unreleased body mixes entries with and without a blank line between them (26 joined directly and 41 blank-separated, counted on 2026-11-11), because each role formats its entry by hand.
- slicer's own `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog with `### Changed` and similar subsections under `## [Unreleased]`; its 1.21.0 entries are bullets joined without blank lines, each ending with the item ID in parentheses, highest ID first. An entry therefore needs a category as well as its text.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-11:

- Q1 format: `landed-changed/ID.md`. The first line is `category: NAME`, where NAME is one of the configured categories, then one blank line, then the entry text in Markdown with no leading bullet. A project that configures no categories writes no category line.
- Q2 assembly: only at release, through `slicer changelog assemble`. Nothing shared changes between releases. (`slicer release` already clears a claim, so the command lives under `changelog`.)
- Q3 writing: `slicer changelog add ID --category C --text TEXT` (or `--stdin`); roles never hand-edit an entry file, and the layout is checked on write.
- Q4 checks: `slicer check` reports a malformed entry file, a file named for an ID with no item, and two files for one item (IDs that differ only in case). A missing entry is a warning only when `changelog_require_entry` is on.
- Q5 conversion: a one-time `slicer changelog import` splits the current Unreleased body into one file per entry.

Settled in this spec (owner to confirm at review): the config key names below; assembly order within a category is highest ID first, matching `CHANGELOG.md` 1.21.0; the missing-entry warning fires at `handoff` and `land`, not in `check`, because `check` cannot tell a released item from an unreleased one once assembly has deleted the files; this repository adopts the feature in the same slice.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/changelog.py` (new; a pure module like `outline.py`: parse an entry file, format the Unreleased body, split an existing Unreleased body into entries; text in, dataclasses out, no I/O).
- `src/slicer/errors.py` (`ChangelogError`, code `changelog_entry`).
- `src/slicer/ops.py` (`changelog_add`, `changelog_assemble`, `changelog_import`, `changelog_problems`, `changelog_missing_entries`: every write goes through here).
- `src/slicer/cli_changelog.py` (new: the three handlers; a module of its own rather than `cli_track.py`, because these commands change no tracking state, take no `--render` and so need none of that module's helpers), `src/slicer/cli_parser.py` (`_add_changelog`) and `src/slicer/cli.py` (`_changes_state`: `changelog` takes the project lock but neither heals the render nor refuses during a merge).
- `src/slicer/config.py` (new keys, below).
- `src/slicer/check.py` (entry-file problems).
- `src/slicer/cli_track.py` (`cmd_handoff` and `cmd_land` print the opt-in missing-entry warning on stderr; `src/slicer/land.py` stays as it is, because the warning is the CLI's stderr and `Landing.to_dict` must gain nothing).
- `tests/test_changelog.py` (new).
- `docs/commands.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/agents.md` (the JSON of the three subcommands), `ARCHITECTURE.md` (the module lists).
- `.slicer/config.json` through `slicer config` (this repository's own settings).
- `CHANGELOG.md` (the header sentence that says unreleased changes belong under `[Unreleased]` now names `landed-changed/`), and this slice's own entry as `landed-changed/` + its ID + `.md`.
- `README.md` (one line on the folder).

Config keys, all in `.slicer/config.json`:

- `changelog_path`, default `""`. Empty turns the feature off: every `changelog` subcommand refuses with code `changelog_off` and says which key to set, and `check` reads no entry files.
- `changelog_entries_dir`, default `"landed-changed"`, relative to the project root.
- `changelog_unreleased_heading`, default `"## [Unreleased]"`; matched as a whole line.
- `changelog_categories`, default `[]`. The order is the order subsections are written in. Empty means no category line and no subsections.
- `changelog_require_entry`, default `false`.

This repository sets `changelog_path` to `CHANGELOG.md` and `changelog_categories` to `["Added", "Changed", "Deprecated", "Removed", "Fixed", "Security"]`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `tests/test_changelog.py`, each on a temp project fixture:

- `test_ChangelogAdd_WritesCategoryLineAndText`: `changelog add s01 --category Changed --text "x"` writes `category: Changed`, a blank line, `x` and a final newline to the entry file. Fails first: no such command.
- `test_ChangelogAdd_UnknownCategory_IsRefused`: a category not in `changelog_categories` exits 2 with code `changelog_category` and writes nothing.
- `test_ChangelogAdd_ExistingEntry_RefusedUnlessReplace`: a second `add` for one item exits 2 with code `changelog_entry_exists`; with `--replace` it overwrites.
- `test_ChangelogAdd_UnknownItem_IsRefused`: `no_such_item`, nothing written.
- `test_ChangelogAdd_Off_IsRefused`: with `changelog_path` empty, code `changelog_off`.
- `test_ChangelogEntries_TwoBranches_MergeWithoutConflict`: in a fixture git repo, two branches each `add` an entry for a different item; `git merge` of the second into the first exits 0 with no conflict.
- `test_ChangelogAssemble_GroupsByCategoryInConfigOrder_HighestIdFirst`: entries for s01 Fixed, s03 Changed and s02 Changed give `### Changed` (s03 then s02) before `### Fixed` (s01) under the Unreleased heading, bullets joined with no blank line, one blank line around each subsection heading; the entry files are deleted.
- `test_ChangelogAssemble_NoCategories_FlatList`: with `changelog_categories` empty, the bullets go straight under the heading.
- `test_ChangelogAssemble_MultiLineEntry_IndentsContinuation`: an entry of two lines is written as `- ` plus line one, then line two indented two spaces.
- `test_ChangelogAssemble_DryRun_PrintsSameBytesAndWritesNothing`: `--dry-run` prints the new changelog text; run twice, the output is byte-identical, and nothing on disk changed.
- `test_ChangelogAssemble_NonEmptyUnreleased_IsRefused`: when the Unreleased body already holds an entry, exits 2 with code `changelog_unreleased_not_empty`, naming `slicer changelog import`.
- `test_ChangelogAssemble_NoHeading_IsRefused`: a changelog without the configured heading line exits 2 with code `changelog_no_heading` and names the file.
- `test_ChangelogImport_MixedLayout_OneFilePerEntry`: an Unreleased body with blank-separated and joined bullets, a multi-line bullet and two category subsections gives one file per bullet, named by the item ID the bullet ends with in parentheses, else `entry-001.md`, `entry-002.md` in body order; the Unreleased body is left empty.
- `test_ChangelogImport_ThenAssemble_GivesTheSameEntries`: import then assemble gives the same set of (category, text) entries as the original body, in the assembled layout.
- `test_ChangelogImport_IsAllOrNothing`: a bullet that sits under a heading that is not a configured category, or an ID file that already exists, refuses the whole import and writes nothing.
- `test_Check_MalformedEntry_NamesTheFile`: a file whose first line is not `category: ` plus a configured category makes `slicer check` exit 1 with a problem naming the file and line 1.
- `test_Check_EntryForUnknownId_IsAProblem` and `test_Check_TwoFilesForOneItem_IsAProblem` (`s01.md` and `S01.md`).
- `test_Check_EntryNamedEntryNnn_IsAccepted`: an imported `entry-001.md` is not a problem.
- `test_Handoff_NoEntry_WarnsOnlyWhenRequired`: with `changelog_require_entry` on, `handoff` prints a stderr warning naming the missing file and still succeeds; with it off, no warning. The same for `land`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first; confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. `changelog.py`: dataclasses `Entry(name, category, text)` with `to_dict`/`from_dict`; `parse_entry(name, text, categories)` that raises with the file and line; `format_unreleased(entries, categories)`; `split_unreleased(body, categories)` for import. No I/O.
3. Config keys in `config.py` with validation (`changelog_categories` a list of nonempty unique strings), documented in `docs/configuration.md`.
4. `ops.changelog_add`, `ops.changelog_assemble(dry_run)`, `ops.changelog_import`: under the writer lock like other writes; import and assemble collect every problem and refuse before writing anything; write the changelog atomically through the same helper other writes use.
5. CLI: `slicer changelog add ID --category C (--text T | --stdin) [--replace]`, `slicer changelog assemble [--dry-run]`, `slicer changelog import [--dry-run]`, each with `--json`. Add them to `docs/commands.md` and the JSON to `docs/agents.md`.
6. `check.py`: entry-file problems when `changelog_path` is set.
7. `handoff` and `land`: the opt-in warning on stderr; the JSON reply gains nothing.
8. Set this repository's config through `slicer config`; reword the `CHANGELOG.md` header sentence; write this slice's own entry with `slicer changelog add`.

Owner decisions (2026-11-11): Who runs the two `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer ...` Check commands? -> assign to orchestrator: the implementer runs the three unittest and `git status --short` checks. The orchestrator or gate runs `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check` (expect exit 0) and `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer changelog assemble --dry-run` (expect the output to show this slice's entry under `### Added`, and `git status --short` unchanged before and after). Both start with an environment assignment, so the brief classes them orchestrator-only..

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests -k Changelog` passes.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` passes.
- `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check` exits 0 on this repository, with this slice's entry file present.
- `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer changelog assemble --dry-run` on this repository prints the changelog with this slice's entry under `### Added` and leaves the working tree unchanged (`git status --short` is the same before and after).
- Mutation: assemble lowest ID first; `test_ChangelogAssemble_GroupsByCategoryInConfigOrder_HighestIdFirst` goes red.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "changelog: per-slice entries in landed-changed/, assembled at release".
